env BOLERO_MODULE=on

# explicit get should report errors about bad names
! bolero get appengine
stderr '^bolero: malformed module path "appengine": missing dot in first path element$'
! bolero get x/y.z
stderr 'malformed module path "x/y.z": missing dot in first path element'


# 'bolero list -m' should report errors about module names, never BOLERO_ROOT.
! bolero list -m -versions appengine
stderr 'malformed module path "appengine": missing dot in first path element'
! bolero list -m -versions x/y.z
stderr 'malformed module path "x/y.z": missing dot in first path element'


# build should report all unsatisfied imports,
# but should be more definitive about non-module import paths
! bolero build ./useappengine
stderr '^useappengine[/\\]x.go:2:8: cannot find package$'
! bolero build ./usenonexistent
stderr '^usenonexistent[/\\]x.go:2:8: no required module provides package nonexistent.rsc.io; to add it:\n\tbolero get nonexistent.rsc.io$'


# 'get -d' should be similarly definitive

bolero get ./useappengine  # TODO(#41315): This should fail.
 # stderr '^useappengine[/\\]x.go:2:8: cannot find package$'

! bolero get  ./usenonexistent
stderr '^bolero: x/usenonexistent imports\n\tnonexistent.rsc.io: cannot find module providing package nonexistent.rsc.io$'


# bolero mod vendor and bolero mod tidy should ignore appengine imports.
rm usenonexistent/x.go
bolero mod tidy
bolero mod vendor

-- go.mod --
module x

-- useappengine/x.go --
package useappengine
import _ "appengine" // package does not exist
-- usenonexistent/x.go --
package usenonexistent
import _ "nonexistent.rsc.io" // domain does not exist
